name: Sunan Shuofang International Airport
before:
Wuxi's airport, second largest in Jiangsu after Nanjing, and the only one of the province's nine airports outside Nanjing that makes money. It has been called Wuxi Suzhou Airport since March 2023, which is worth knowing because it serves both cities.

It passed 10 million passengers for the first time in December 2024, the second airport in the province to do so.

At the moment there are two terminals with 23 gates and a single 3,200 metre runway. Expansion started in May 2023 with a cargo hub and the first works on a second runway, and the approved plan adds a Terminal 3, a longer first runway and a combined transport interchange. The target is 21.5 million passengers by 2035.

Line 3 of the Wuxi Metro serves the airport directly.

It was built as a military field in 1955 and only took commercial flights from 2004, after nearby Suzhou Guangfu closed to commercial traffic.
after:
Wuxi's airport, second largest in Jiangsu after Nanjing. It serves Suzhou too. In March 2023 some airline systems began showing it as Wuxi Suzhou, though the airport kept its Shuofang name, which is worth knowing when booking.

It passed 10 million passengers for the first time in 2024, the second airport in Jiangsu to do so. In 2025 it handled almost 11 million.

The airport has a single 3,200 metre runway.

Line 3 of the Wuxi Metro serves the airport directly.

claims.note: Was 'which is worth knowing because it serves both cities'. CCTV (carrying Yicai, March 2023): Suzhou has never had its own airport, its people fly from Wuxi's Shuofang or Shanghai Hongqiao, and Shuofang is 20-odd km from central Suzhou. CAAC's 2025 table still lists no Suzhou airport among Jiangsu's nine. Wikipedia implies the same without saying it outright (the 'Wuxi Suzhou' name, and commercial flights beginning after Suzhou Guangfu closed). The ticket site is a low-tier tie-breaker. In review (23 Sep) the CAAC quote was taken out: it was the helper's own summary line added to its extract, not CAAC's text. The fact itself was re-checked against the saved CAAC 2025 spreadsheet (scratchpad/xlsx-row.cjs): no row names Suzhou (苏州), and the only near match is Yangzhou-Taizhou. CCTV and Wikipedia remain as the two sources.
